eyebrow: AN ENGINEERING FRAMEWORK FOR HUMAN–AGENT COLLABORATION
title:
Maker-Orchestrated
Engineering
subtitle: Human Vision. Intelligent Execution. Verified Outcomes.
notes: Introduce MOE as a proposed operating model, not an autonomous coding product or an industry certification. Its purpose is to make accountability, authorization, delegation, evidence and learning explicit when intelligent agents participate in engineering. This presentation is vendor-neutral. Organizations keep their lifecycle and tools. No productivity improvement is claimed without a pilot.

title:
More generated work is not
the same as more delivered value.
subtitle: The system must scale understanding, verification and responsibility—not only implementation.

cards.title: Intent
cards.body: What outcome is worth pursuing?

cards.title: Authority
cards.body: What may people and agents do?

cards.title: Evidence
cards.body: What supports acceptance?

cards.title: Learning
cards.body: Did the change actually help?

notes: This is the problem statement and design motivation, not a quantitative research claim. A faster implementation step can still create downstream review and operational work. MOE focuses on the complete system of delivery. GitHub’s November 6, 2026 article provides related lifecycle framing across planning, building, verifying and observing; it does not validate MOE or establish its benefits. See reference 3.

title:
Human accountability.
Bounded intelligent execution.
subtitle: MOE is a vendor-neutral, lifecycle-adaptable framework for responsible collaboration between people and intelligent agents.

cards.title: The maker
cards.body: Owns technical coherence and responsible orchestration.

cards.title: The organization
cards.body: Retains business, policy and release authority.

cards.title: The agents
cards.body: Investigate, propose and execute bounded work.

notes: The maker is an accountability, not a mandatory job title or a renamed manager. The maker may still write code, debug, design and test. The role does not absorb all business, security or release decisions. Agents are execution resources and can recommend decisions; they cannot create their own authority.

title:
A collaboration framework.
Not another mandatory lifecycle.
notes: MOE does not require abandoning an effective existing process. It complements the organization’s lifecycle by making human-agent collaboration explicit. It is not a claim that Agile is obsolete. The Agile Manifesto and Scrum Guide are background sources, not endorsements or documents modified by MOE. See references 1 and 2.

title: Seven principles. One direction.
notes: These are proposed preferences that guide tradeoffs. They are not permission to ignore documentation, security or existing policy. The seventh principle is important: agents can propose better instructions or shared knowledge, but promotion into trusted context requires review. The manifesto is a working draft and should be challenged through adoption experience.

title:
Standardize the meaning.
Let organizations choose the machinery.
layers: Map capabilities to the existing development process
Human-led • one agent • several bounded agents
Work systems • source • execution • evidence • delivery
notes: The core sets invariants. Profiles map them into an organization. Adapters implement integration choices. A profile can strengthen core requirements, but cannot silently remove them and still claim full core conformance. No particular model, cloud, language, IDE, scanner or tool protocol is mandatory.

title: An operating loop, not six new meetings.
subtitle: Capabilities can overlap and repeat. Existing lifecycle states remain usable.
notes: The loop is a conceptual map rather than a rigid waterfall. A discovery mission can produce a design or assessment instead of code. Technical acceptance, delivery and outcome observation are distinct states. Scope, acceptance or policy changes require reassessment of affected approvals and evidence. The term Prove means evaluate scoped evidence, not establish universal correctness.

title:
Five logical records.
Not five new tools.
items: What outcome and boundaries are authorized?
Who decided what, on which basis?
subtitle: For a small change, one existing work item may hold all five.
notes: The contract types define semantics, not a storage architecture. The mission identifies intent, scope, acceptance and observation. Delegation narrows the assignment. Policy governs authority. The proof bundle binds evidence to the candidate. Decision records preserve accountable approval, rejection and exceptions. They can coexist in a ticket or be separate controlled records.

title:
MOE governs the work.
ECS makes it understandable.
notes: The MOE project adopts Engineering Clarity Standard (ECS) for newly written and revised technical prose. Other organizations may use an equivalent standard: ECS is recommended, not a core-conformance requirement. A skill can improve wording but cannot authorize an action, enforce a permission, or establish software correctness. Contract schemas validate structure; trusted verification supplies evidence. The imported ECS 1.0.0 skill is pinned to commit 871dbf7030cf18be6312fb0fca00b86d440f7a98, with its MIT license preserved. It is not formal ASD-STE100 compliance. See implementation/ecs-integration.md and reference 7.

title:
Clear language across
all five contracts.
items: Actor, outcome, scope and open questions
Exact task, constraints and stop conditions
Actual results, missing evidence and uncertainty
Authority, scope, rationale and unresolved risk
subtitle: Repository default. Optional for adopters. Never a substitute for evidence.
notes: Requirements analysts, planners, implementers, reviewers and documentation authors share the same writing guidance. A dedicated clarity agent is optional, not the only owner of understandable work. Each subagent needs the relevant skill and glossary in its own context. Preserve identifiers, schema keys, raw logs and tool results. Missing results mean unknown unless non-execution is known; only then use not_run. The package contains integrity checks, a heuristic writing checker and ten evaluation cases. Automated checks do not demonstrate that an IDE loaded the skill or that a model followed it. Runtime activation and behavioral evaluations remain not_run. Sources: the pinned ECS skill and MOE integration guide.

title:
The maker owns technical coherence.
Not everybody else’s authority.
notes: Organizations map these responsibilities to their existing roles. Several responsibilities can belong to one person where policy permits. Required separation of duties still applies. The planner or lead agent is not an approval authority simply because it coordinates work. Teams should provide an explicit accountability-transfer process when a maker is unavailable.

title: Keep authority outside the model.
subtitle: Models propose. The host checks authority. Controlled tools act. Trusted systems produce evidence.
bottom: Work systems, source, tests, delivery and knowledge remain behind approved adapters.
notes: This is a reference design, not a required centralized platform. The control plane owns authorization, budgets, transitions and cancellation. Executors receive scoped access and cannot alter their own policy. Command allowlisting alone is not a sandbox because builds can run repository-controlled code. No tool transport eliminates the need for access control, isolation, validation and auditing.

title:
“The agent says it passed”
is not an acceptance gate.
items: Mission revision + policy revision + exact candidate
Actual runs + artifacts + producers + relevant environment
Every required acceptance condition to evidence
Authorized acceptance with limitations and exceptions
subtitle: A second model’s agreement is review—not execution evidence.
notes: Proof bundles support a decision within a stated scope. They do not prove absence of defects. Record passed, failed, not_run, unknown and not_applicable distinctly. Hashes identify bytes but do not authenticate producers by themselves. Material changes to candidate, merge context, dependencies, configuration or policy require reassessment of affected evidence. Delivery and demonstrated business value remain separate.

title:
Autonomy is an action policy.
Not a confidence score.
subtitle: Illustrative levels only. Deny by default. Recheck authority. Support revocation.
notes: These levels are optional labels. Actual permissions must specify subject, action, resource, environment, data scope, expiry and approval conditions. Better model performance does not automatically increase rights. Some organizations permit automated low-risk delivery; others retain manual authorization. Neither choice changes the need for human accountability, bounded permissions and independently enforced gates. OWASP provides related least-privilege guidance; see reference 5.

title: Adopt MOE without surrendering your process.

cards.title: Scrum-oriented
cards.body: Backlog item + existing accountabilities + Definition of Done evidence.

cards.title: Kanban-oriented
cards.body: Explicit policies + WIP limits + review-capacity-aware flow.

cards.title: Continuous delivery
cards.body: Small candidates + enforced gates + progressive observation.

cards.title: Formal governance
cards.body: Controlled baselines + attributable approvals + retained evidence.

notes: These are illustrative mappings, not official modifications to the named practices. Teams choose profile details and retain applicable obligations. A regulated profile is not a compliance certification. A profile can add controls, but cannot remove a core requirement without disclosing partial adoption.

title: One small mission makes the model concrete.
steps: Bound page size for a catalog request.
Sandbox edits only; no merge or production writes.
Two acceptance conditions; checks explicitly not run.
After a separately authorized release, measure effects.
subtitle: The repository fixtures demonstrate structure. They do not claim application success.
notes: The example is intentionally incomplete at the acceptance stage. It has a synthetic maker, policy, delegation and authorization record. Required application checks remain not_run. The reference validator can verify these records are structurally consistent without pretending that a catalog application was built, tested or deployed. This distinction is essential to the framework’s credibility.

title: Start with a controlled experiment.
subtitle: One team. A low-risk area. Existing standards. Explicit stop conditions.
notes: This sequence is a suggested pilot design, not a promised schedule. Predeclare the hypothesis, approved data, review capacity, budget, quality thresholds and stop criteria. Include failed and cancelled work. Pause on unauthorized actions, evidence tampering or failed controls. A small pilot can reveal feasibility and problems without proving general superiority.

title:
Measure the whole system.
Keep the scorecard multidimensional.

cards.title: Delivery
cards.body: Accepted-delivery lead time and throughput.

cards.title: Attention
cards.body: Review time, queue age and rework.

cards.title: Quality
cards.body: Defects, incidents and maintainability.

cards.title: Control
cards.body: Unauthorized actions and evidence gaps.

cards.title: Economics
cards.body: Human effort, compute and total cost.

cards.title: Outcomes
cards.body: Observed user or business effects.

notes: Do not replace story-point theater with token-count theater. Report comparable work classes, sample size, distributions and observation windows. Separate technically accepted delivery from confirmed outcomes. Do not rank people by raw mission counts. Use baseline or matched comparisons and disclose confounders. The framework makes no numerical ROI claim.

title:
Evidence-backed self-assessment.
Not a certification badge.

cards.title: Exploring
cards.body: Trying selected concepts; no core claim.

cards.title: Partial adoption
cards.body: Mapped implementation with visible gaps.

cards.title: Self-assessed core conformance
cards.body: C01–C10 assessed for an explicit scope and version.

subtitle: A schema-valid record does not establish a valid approval, enforced control or safe release.
notes: A declaration must identify version, assessed team and environments, dates, evidence, exceptions and limitations. Review representative successes and failures and exercise negative paths. This project does not run a certification program. The reference validator checks structure and selected cross-record invariants only.

title: Build credibility before claiming maturity.
steps: Review the foundation and open decisions
Run a bounded pilot and publish sanitized findings
Stabilize semantics, review evidence and document limits
subtitle: Licensed under Apache-2.0. Governance approval is still an owner decision. No adoption results are claimed.
notes: The repository includes core documents, schemas, synthetic examples, templates, lifecycle profiles, implementation guidance, validation and presentation source. It does not include a production orchestration platform. The project is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. Seek feedback from engineering, product, security and operations across more than one organizational context.

title:
Make intent clear.
Bound the work.
Verify the outcome.
subtitle: Pilot the framework. Challenge the assumptions. Improve it with evidence.
tag: Human Vision. Intelligent Execution. Verified Outcomes.
notes: Ask the audience to review whether the contracts are useful, identify missing controls, and choose a safe pilot rather than endorse an untested enterprise rollout. The goal is a portable engineering framework that preserves human understanding and responsibility while making intelligent execution useful.
